task_1.title: Remove unnecessary numpy dependency from pytest.approx failure representation
task_1.description: When pytest.approx was used to compare sequences and the assertion failed, the failure representation code imported numpy to use np.inf. If numpy was not installed, this caused a ModuleNotFoundError during failure message rendering, which obscured the actual assertion error with a confusing 'faulty __repr__' message. The fix replaces the numpy dependency with the equivalent standard library math.inf, so that pytest.approx failure messages render correctly without numpy installed.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that pytest.approx produces a clear and complete assertion failure message when comparing sequences, even when numpy is not installed. Previously, a failing approximate sequence comparison would raise a ModuleNotFoundError for numpy during error representation, hiding the actual comparison details and confusing users into thinking numpy was a required dependency.

expectation.grounded: When an assertion using pytest.approx on sequences (e.g., lists) fails and numpy is not installed, the ApproxSequenceLike._repr_compare method must render the full comparison diff without raising ModuleNotFoundError. The method must use math.inf from the standard library instead of numpy.inf when computing the maximum relative difference for zero-valued entries. The observable output should show the per-element comparison details, absolute differences, and relative differences, with no 'faulty __repr__' fallback message.
expectation.conceptual: When a pytest.approx sequence comparison fails, the assertion error output must always display the full element-by-element comparison details regardless of whether numpy is installed. The error representation must never trigger an import error for an optional third-party package.

constraints.grounded: The infinity value used for relative difference computation when the other value is zero must remain semantically equivalent (math.inf behaves identically to numpy.inf for float comparisons). No numpy import must remain in the ApproxSequenceLike._repr_compare method. The comparison logic, tolerance computation, and diff formatting must remain unchanged. Existing behavior when numpy IS installed must not regress.
constraints.conceptual: The fix must not alter any comparison logic or tolerance semantics of pytest.approx. The change must only affect the failure message rendering path and must not introduce any new dependencies. All existing pytest.approx behavior for sequences must be preserved.

behavior: When pytest.approx compares two sequences and they differ beyond tolerance, the failure representation no longer imports numpy.
When the compared-against value is zero, the maximum relative difference is set to positive infinity using the standard library math module instead of numpy.
Failure messages for approximate sequence comparisons now render successfully without numpy installed, showing per-element expected vs actual values, absolute differences, and relative differences.
The 'representation of details failed ... ModuleNotFoundError: No module named numpy ... Probably an object has a faulty __repr__' error no longer appears in assertion output when numpy is absent.
acceptance_criteria: When numpy is NOT installed and a test asserts a list equals pytest.approx(another_list) and the values differ beyond tolerance, the assertion error output should display the full element-by-element comparison with expected and actual values, not a ModuleNotFoundError.
When numpy IS installed, the pytest.approx sequence comparison failure output should remain identical to previous behavior.
When comparing a sequence where one of the actual values is 0.0 against a non-zero expected value, the relative difference should correctly reflect infinity in the failure output.

Given a test like 'assert [1, 2] == pytest.approx([1.001, 2.002])' in an environment without numpy, when the test fails, the output should show the per-element approximation details without any 'faulty __repr__' warning.

task_2.title: Fix assertion diff crash on dataclasses with InitVar fields
task_2.description: When an assertion comparing two dataclass instances with InitVar fields fails, pytest's assertion introspection crashes with an AttributeError instead of displaying a useful diff. This happens because the diff-generation logic enumerates all entries in the internal __dataclass_fields__ mapping, which includes InitVar fields that are not stored as instance attributes. The fix switches to the public dataclasses.fields() API, which only returns actual instance fields, thereby skipping InitVar entries and producing a correct comparison diff.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that when an assertion comparing two dataclass instances fails, pytest produces a detailed field-by-field diff even when the dataclass declares one or more InitVar fields. Previously, the assertion introspection would crash with an AttributeError (reported as 'representation of details failed') because it attempted to read InitVar fields as regular instance attributes.

expectation.grounded: The _compare_eq_cls helper in the assertion utilities must enumerate dataclass fields using dataclasses.fields() rather than the raw __dataclass_fields__ mapping. This ensures InitVar fields—which are present in __dataclass_fields__ but absent from the instance—are excluded from the comparison loop. When two unequal dataclass instances with InitVar fields are compared in an assert statement, pytest should emit a per-field diff for each real (non-InitVar) field that differs, with no AttributeError or 'representation of details failed' fallback message.
expectation.conceptual: When a failing assertion compares two dataclass objects that use InitVar fields, pytest must display a clean, field-by-field diff of only the actual stored attributes. The assertion introspection must not crash or fall back to a degraded error message due to the presence of init-only variables.

constraints.grounded: The fix must not alter assertion diff behavior for dataclasses without InitVar fields. Dataclass fields with compare=False must still be excluded from the diff. The attrs-based dataclass comparison path must remain unchanged. The change must use the public dataclasses.fields() API rather than internal dunder attributes for field enumeration.
constraints.conceptual: Existing assertion diff output for standard dataclasses and attrs classes must not regress. Only init-only variable fields should be newly excluded; all other field filtering rules (such as opting out of comparison) must continue to work as before.

behavior: dataclasses.fields() is used to enumerate dataclass fields for assertion diff generation, which inherently excludes InitVar fields since they are not returned by that API.
Field names for comparison are extracted from the field descriptor objects returned by dataclasses.fields(), filtering on the compare attribute.
When comparing dataclass instances with InitVar fields in a failed assertion, pytest no longer raises an AttributeError when attempting to access init-only variables on the instance.
The per-field diff output only includes real instance attributes, correctly omitting InitVar declarations.
acceptance_criteria: When a failing assertion compares two dataclass instances that declare one or more InitVar fields, pytest should display a field-by-field diff of only the real stored attributes without any error or fallback message.
When a failing assertion compares two standard dataclass instances (no InitVar), the diff output should be identical to the previous behavior.
When a dataclass field has compare=False, it should still be excluded from the assertion diff regardless of whether InitVar fields are present.
When a failing assertion compares two attrs-based class instances, the diff behavior should remain unchanged.
Given a dataclass with both InitVar fields and regular fields where some regular fields differ, the diff should list only the differing regular fields and must not reference any InitVar field.

task_3.title: Fix NODE_CTOR_FSPATH_ARG deprecation warning stacklevel to point to user code
task_3.description: The NODE_CTOR_FSPATH_ARG deprecation warning, which is emitted when users pass the legacy fspath (py.path.local) argument instead of the modern path (pathlib.Path) argument to node constructors, was pointing to an internal pytest frame rather than the user's actual call site. This made it difficult for users to identify which line in their own code triggered the deprecation. The stacklevel was corrected so the warning now accurately references the user's code where the deprecated fspath argument is passed.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that the NODE_CTOR_FSPATH_ARG deprecation warning emitted by pytest node constructors points to the user's own code (the call site passing the deprecated fspath argument), rather than pointing to an internal pytest source location. Previously, the warning traceback referenced an internal pytest frame, making it unclear to users which line of their code needed to be updated to replace fspath with path.

expectation.grounded: When a user invokes a Node subclass constructor or its from_parent class method with the deprecated fspath argument, the resulting PytestRemovedIn8Warning should have its stacklevel set so that the warning's reported file and line number correspond to the user's call site (e.g., the line calling SomeNode.from_parent(parent, fspath=...)), not an internal frame within _imply_path or Node._create. The _imply_path helper function must emit the NODE_CTOR_FSPATH_ARG deprecation with a stacklevel that traverses the full internal call chain back to user code.
expectation.conceptual: When pytest emits a deprecation warning about the legacy fspath argument on node constructors, the warning message should identify the exact location in the user's own test code or plugin code that needs to be updated. Users should be able to read the warning and immediately know which line to change without having to trace through pytest internals.

constraints.grounded: The fix must only affect the stacklevel of the NODE_CTOR_FSPATH_ARG deprecation warning within the _imply_path function. The warning message text, warning category (PytestRemovedIn8Warning), and the conditions under which the warning is triggered must remain unchanged. The deprecation must still fire whenever fspath is provided and path is not, regardless of whether the node is instantiated directly or via from_parent.
constraints.conceptual: The change must not suppress, alter the content of, or change the triggering conditions for the deprecation warning. Only the reported source location of the warning should change. All existing deprecation behavior and warning filtering must continue to work as before.

behavior: The NODE_CTOR_FSPATH_ARG deprecation warning now reports the file and line number of the user's code that passes the deprecated fspath argument to a Node constructor or from_parent call.
Previously, the warning pointed to an internal pytest frame (e.g., inside the _create or _imply_path call), which was not actionable for users.
The warning category (PytestRemovedIn8Warning), message format, and trigger conditions remain identical; only the reported source location has changed.
This affects all Node subclass constructors (Item, Collector, File, etc.) that go through the _imply_path path-resolution logic when the deprecated fspath argument is supplied.
acceptance_criteria: When a test or plugin calls Node.from_parent(parent, fspath=some_path) using the deprecated fspath argument, the resulting deprecation warning should report the file and line of that from_parent call, not an internal pytest file.
When a custom Node subclass is instantiated directly with the fspath keyword argument, the deprecation warning should point to the line of user code performing the instantiation.
The warning message must still contain the node type name and the standard NODE_CTOR_FSPATH_ARG deprecation text.
The warning category must remain PytestRemovedIn8Warning.
When the path argument is provided instead of fspath, no deprecation warning should be emitted (existing behavior preserved).
Warning filters (e.g., filterwarnings in pytest configuration) that match on PytestRemovedIn8Warning must continue to function correctly with the updated stacklevel.

task_4.title: Fix tmp_path fixture crash when getpass module is not importable
task_4.description: In rare environments (e.g., when running with certain coverage tools or in sandboxed/exotic setups), the standard library module getpass may fail to import. The get_user() helper used by the tmp_path fixture already had a try/except to handle failures from getpass.getuser(), but the import getpass statement itself was placed outside the try block. This meant a ModuleNotFoundError during import propagated as an unhandled internal error during fixture setup, preventing any test that used tmp_path or tmp_path_factory from running. The fix moves the import inside the try block so that import failures are caught alongside runtime failures, and get_user() gracefully returns None.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that the tmp_path fixture does not raise an internal error during setup when the getpass standard library module cannot be imported. In exotic or restricted environments (e.g., certain coverage tool configurations), importing getpass may fail with a ModuleNotFoundError. Previously this crashed the fixture; the get_user() helper must handle this gracefully.

expectation.grounded: The get_user() function must catch ImportError (and its subclass ModuleNotFoundError) raised during the import of getpass, in addition to the already-handled ImportError and KeyError from getpass.getuser(). When the import fails, get_user() must return None. The TempPathFactory.getbasetemp() method should then use the fallback username string and proceed normally, allowing tmp_path and tmp_path_factory fixtures to complete setup without error.
expectation.conceptual: When the tmp_path fixture attempts to determine the current username and the underlying system module is unavailable, the fixture should fall back to a default username and continue operating normally. No internal error should be raised to the user; temporary directory creation should succeed regardless of whether the username can be resolved.

constraints.grounded: The existing handling of KeyError from getpass.getuser() (for environments where the user is not determinable at runtime) must remain intact. The get_user() function must continue to return Optional[str], returning the username string on success and None on any failure. The except clause must cover both ImportError and KeyError as before. No new exceptions should be suppressed beyond what was already intended.
constraints.conceptual: The fix must not change the behavior for the common case where the username is successfully resolved. Error handling should remain narrowly scoped to known failure modes of username retrieval, not broadly suppress unrelated exceptions. The temporary directory creation workflow must remain fully functional in both normal and degraded environments.

behavior: When getpass cannot be imported (e.g., ModuleNotFoundError), get_user() returns None instead of raising an unhandled exception.
When getpass is importable but getpass.getuser() raises KeyError, get_user() continues to return None as before.
When getpass is importable and getpass.getuser() succeeds, get_user() returns the username string as before.
The tmp_path and tmp_path_factory fixtures complete setup successfully even in environments where getpass is not importable, using a fallback username for the base temporary directory path.
No change in behavior for the normal case where getpass is available and the user is resolvable.
acceptance_criteria: When the getpass module is not importable, using the tmp_path fixture in a test should not raise any error during fixture setup.
When the getpass module is not importable, get_user() should return None.
When getpass is importable but getpass.getuser() raises KeyError, get_user() should return None.
When getpass is importable and getpass.getuser() succeeds, get_user() should return the username string.

Given a test using tmp_path in an environment where getpass cannot be imported, when the test runs, then the temporary directory is created successfully with a fallback username component in the path.
Given a normal environment where getpass works correctly, when a test uses tmp_path, then behavior is identical to before the fix.
